subject: Vertex Health — private access options and non-functional requirements
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@vertexhealth.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vertex Health Network Team <netops@vertexhealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment connectivity — short brief and constraints

Evelyn,

Thanks again for the onboarding call last week. We are scoping a private deployment of Redwood in our VPC and the security/compliance team asked for a concise recommendation on connectivity modes (VPC Peering, AWS PrivateLink, or a site-to-site VPN) for production inference traffic. High-level constraints from our side:

- HIPAA scope: no public internet egress for inference traffic; audit logs required.
- IP address hygiene: we cannot allow transitive routing across our enterprise VPCs.
- CIDR overlaps are possible (we’ll share ranges).
- Prefer minimal changes to existing route tables and minimal NAT reliance.
- Need TLS mutual auth for control-plane and optional metrics streaming.

Attached is a quick spreadsheet with estimated qps, payload sizes, and the list of subnets we plan to use (vertex_requirements.xlsx). Can your team sketch the tradeoffs and an initial mutual action plan?

Primary contact for netops is netops@vertexhealth.com (cc'd).

Best,
Sam
Lead Cloud Network Architect
Vertex Health

Attachments: vertex_requirements.xlsx (Excel spreadsheet)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-17T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity — short brief and constraints

Sam — thanks for the clear constraints and the spreadsheet. We can definitely do a short recommendation and MAP.

Quick ask before we dive deep: can you confirm whether the inference callers will be inside a single VPC (singe-project) or multiple VPCs across accounts? That influences peering feasibility.

Initial thoughts (very high level):
- PrivateLink gives you strong endpoint isolation and no transitive routing — good for strict HIPAA boundaries and avoids CIDR conflicts, but it can be more operationally complex for a high fan-out of internal callers.
- VPC Peering is simpler and low-latency when CIDRs don’t overlap, but it allows routing between the peered VPCs (transitive routing concerns).
- Site-to-site VPN is flexible and works with on-prem, but typically has higher latency and is less attractive for high-throughput inference unless you put dedicated appliances and BGP in front of it.

Ben, Kim, Jordan — looping you in to add the kernel-level and operations considerations (latency, TLS termination, IP visibility, audit logs). Sam — we’ll aim to get a one-page recommendation + MAP by EOD tomorrow if you can confirm VPC topology.

— Evelyn
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity — short brief and constraints

Evelyn / team — adding a short tech note to help the rec: 

1) Latency & throughput
- VPC Peering: lowest network hop — ideal for sub-10ms intra-region hop if CIDRs clean. Good for high qps inference.
- PrivateLink: adds an endpoint network interface (ENI) and NLB in the provider VPC — adds small but predictable overhead ~1-3ms; scales well behind NLBs but each endpoint is per-service/per-region.
- S2S VPN: variable latency depending on customer gateway and path; jitter and MTU issues common — not preferable for latency-sensitive traffic.

2) Security / traffic visibility
- PrivateLink: only allows connections from the calling VPC to the endpoint — no route table changes, no transitive routing. Good for least-privilege requirement.
- Peering: full L3 adjacency — you need strict route & security group hygiene, and peering does not traverse AWS Transit Gateway unless you design that in.
- VPN: can be isolated but often requires NAT/edge appliances; ensure you have IPsec and support for mTLS on our side.

3) Compliance / logging
- PrivateLink + TLS mTLS: we can terminate and forward logs to your s3 (signed) or push audit events to your SIEM (via secure forwarding).
- Peering: you rely on VPC Flow Logs and our telemetry; need to define SLA for retained audit logs.

4) Ops model & scale
- If Vertex has many caller VPCs: PrivateLink avoids creating O(N) peering relationships but might require deploying and managing endpoint services per region.
- Peering is cheaper in egress cost for high-volume but operationally brittle if IP space overlap exists.

5) Edge cases
- CIDR overlap: PrivateLink wins.
- Transitive routing restrictions: PrivateLink wins.
- Multi-region deployments: both approaches need careful planning; PrivateLink endpoints are regional.

I’ll put these into a one-pager with recommended pilot configuration.

— Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@vertexhealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-17T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity — short brief and constraints

Team / Sam — a couple of procurement and SLA points to flag so the MAP is actionable:

- SLA: Vertex needs to confirm desired uptime and RPO/RTO for inference endpoints. PrivateLink endpoints are subject to our provider-side scaling and have well-defined failure domains; peering depends on underlying infra in the VPCs.
- Key management: if Vertex wants to use their own keys for encryption-in-transit (client certs) we need to validate KMS/HSM integration for control-plane secrets.
- Billing: PrivateLink has endpoint hour and data processing costs; peering data transfer follows inter-AZ/inter-region pricing which may be more economical at large scale. Please confirm expected 95th percentile token throughput so we can model costs.
- Change windows & emergency access: If we need an ops tunnel for debugging, we should define a short-lived S2S VPN or a bastion flow that is audited.

Sam — if HIPAA scope requires a separate private control plane, we should note that in the MAP (Private offering supports a private control plane; on-prem option possible for air-gapped deployments).

Thanks — I’ll add a short cost table to the one-pager.

— Kim
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@vertexhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-18T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity — short brief and constraints

Thanks — good notes. To be explicit on a few items so your MAP is actionable: 

- Topology: inference callers will be from a single "vertex-core" VPC in our production account (we may later onboard additional VPCs in other accounts).
- Throughput: expect sustained 300 qps with peaks at 1200 qps; median payload size ~2KB.
- CIDR: our prod VPC uses 10.0.0.0/16 — we are willing to carve /24s for peering only if necessary.
- Compliance: HIPAA requires we avoid transitive routing unless explicitly tested and approved.
- Ops tunnel: we want a procedure for ephemeral access for debugging (timeboxed and logged).

Given this: we are leaning toward PrivateLink for initial launch to avoid CIDR overlap and transitive routing. We are open to a dedicated peering relationship later if costs demand. Please include a minimal pilot plan (steps, owners, tentative timeline) and a short checklist of the exact artifacts we need to produce for our security team (certs, flow logs, audit export).

— Sam

Date: 2026-08-18T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment connectivity — short brief and constraints (Recommendation + MAP)

Sam — thanks for the extra detail. Attached are the deliverables: 1) a one-page recommendation (summary below), 2) redwood_privatelink_playbook.pdf (implementation checklist), and 3) a draft mutual-action-plan (mutual-action-plan-vertex.txt).

Recommendation (pilot):
- Pilot using AWS PrivateLink for inference traffic in us-west-2. Rationale: avoids CIDR overlap, enforces no-transitive-routing, supports per-endpoint access controls required for HIPAA.
- Use PrivateLink for the inference API surface (tokenized requests + streaming). Deploy a dedicated endpoint service behind an NLB in our provider VPC and expose only the required ports.
- For ops/debugging and emergency maintenance, provision a timeboxed site-to-site VPN with strict ACLs and a jump host — this tunnel is only for engineers with mTLS certs and is fully audited.
- Roadmap to peering: if steady-state egress cost and throughput justify it after 3 months (reviewed at the MAP checkpoint), we can add a single VPC Peering connection with restrictive SGs and route filters; only after explicit overlap checks.

Immediate MAP (next 10 business days):
1) Vertex: confirm final CIDR and approve a /28 for endpoint ENIs (if you prefer we can avoid this step and rely on endpoint-managed ENIs). (Owner: Vertex NetOps)
2) Redwood: provide PrivateLink service name, NLB port mapping, and required listener certs. (Owner: Ben)
3) Vertex: provide cert signing key details and confirm KMS integration for control-plane secrets. (Owner: Vertex SecOps)
4) Joint: run a test plan (connectivity smoke test, TLS mTLS handshake, audit log export). (Owner: Jordan + Vertex NetOps)
5) Joint: schedule 2-hour pilot cutover window and rollback plan. (Owner: Evelyn)

Checklist for security team (artifacts we will provide):
- TLS mTLS config guide and public cert fingerprints
- VPC Flow Logs export sample and log retention policy
- Audit log export path and adjacency for SIEM ingestion
- Playbook for emergency S2S tunnel activation (timeboxed + MFA audit)

Next steps: Ben will circulate the cost table; Jordan will prepare the smoke test steps; Kim will draft the SLA language for the pilot. I’ll book a 30-min MAP review tomorrow at 10a PT — netops@vertexhealth.com please confirm availability.

Thanks — we’ll keep the MAP tight and practical.

— Evelyn
Director, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_privatelink_playbook.pdf (PDF checklist), mutual-action-plan-vertex.txt (plain text MAP)
